LESSON: MAPS AND MAP WORK

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Natural and Historic Built Environments in Africa
Topic 4.3: Maps and map work
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Maps and map work, part of Natural and Historic Built Environments in Africa in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How are maps used? 2. Why is time different in various locations?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. describe the position, shape and size of Africa,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Maps and map work in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. locate places and features using latitudes and longitudes on a map,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Maps and map work in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. calculating the time of different places in the world,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Maps and map work in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate the location of key features in the continent. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Maps and map work together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Digital Literacy: Learners apply the skill of designing and creating new digital artefacts, content and materials as they establish

the position and location of places and features on a map.

● Creativity and Imagination: Learners undertake group activities and exchange new ideas that inspire creative thinking as they

draw an outline map of Africa.

Values:
● Responsibility: Learners develop diligence as they research the three types of maps used in Social Studies and make summary

notes.

● Patriotism: Learners develop loyalty as they draw an outline map of Africa and indicate the countries that make up Africa.

● Unity: Learners demonstrate fairness as they brainstorm the position, shape and size of Africa.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Social Cohesion: Learners brainstorm the position, shape and size of Africa.

● Environmental Education: Learners use latitudes to locate the position of places and features on a map.

Link to other learning areas:

Learners apply calculation skills as they use longitudes to calculate time of different places in the world.
